## Purpose

`GHG_Model_SiteMeans.qmd` uses a hand-picked set of five predictors. This
notebook lets the data choose instead. `MuMIn::dredge()` fits every model
built from a pool of candidate predictors, up to a maximum size, and ranks
them by an information criterion.

With n = 48 sites and ~20 candidate predictors there are over a thousand
candidate models, so the best one will look good even if no predictor
matters. The default settings use four safeguards against this:

1. **A screened candidate pool.** Predictors are dropped one at a time until
   every VIF is below a threshold, and strongly correlated pairs may not share
   a model.
2. **Small models.** At most `M_MAX` terms per model.
3. **A permutation test of the whole search.** The response is shuffled and
   dredge is run again many times. That gives the AIC gain of the best model
   over the null that you get when the predictors carry no information. The
   real gain is compared against it.
4. **Nested cross-validation.** Dredge is re-run without each held-out fold,
   and the model it picks predicts that fold. This measures how well the
   *selection procedure* predicts new sites, not just the model it chose.

**Reading the output.** p-values and confidence intervals for the selected
model are too optimistic, because the same data chose the model. Use the
permutation test and the cross-validation to decide whether there is a
signal. Use summed weights and the top-model set to decide which predictors
carry it.

## Settings

All settings that change the analysis are in this chunk. Edit them and
re-render.

```{r settings}
## ============================================================================
## Candidate predictor pool
## ============================================================================
WINDOW <- 10 # raster window (m): 10, 30 or 50

## Raster bands and statistics; each band x stat becomes "<band>_<stat>"
RASTER_BANDS <- c("DEM", "twi", "HAND", "CHM", "TPI", "DMV",
                  "NDVI", "NDWI", "NDVI_lo", "NDWI_lo", "WETprob")
RASTER_STATS <- c("mean", "sd")

## Climate columns from NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv (averaged over the two
## sampling rounds). Short names used in the models: "temperature_2m" ->
## "tmean", "total_precipitation_sum" -> "ppt".
CLIMATE_VARS <- c(
  "prism_ppt_annual",
  "prism_tmean_annual",
  "era5_temperature_2m_14d",
  "era5_total_precipitation_sum_14d"
)

## Hand adjustments to the pool (use the short names, e.g. "DEM_sd")
EXCLUDE <- character() # never in the pool
PROTECT <- character() # always in the pool; the VIF screen won't drop these
FIXED <- character()   # in every model (dredge `fixed =`); also protected

## Interactions to offer dredge, e.g. c("WETprob_mean:NDVI_mean").
## Dredge only fits an interaction alongside both of its main effects, and
## both main effects are protected from the VIF screen. An interaction uses 3
## of the M_MAX terms, so raise M_MAX to 4 to let it sit with another predictor.
INTERACTIONS <- character(3)

## ============================================================================
## Pool screening
## ============================================================================
VIF_MAX <- 10   # drop highest-VIF predictor until all are below this; Inf = off
COR_MAX <- 0.7 # pairs with |Spearman rho| >= this can't share a model; 1 = off

## ============================================================================
## Dredge
## ============================================================================
M_MIN <- 0       # min terms per model (0 = include the null model)
M_MAX <- 5       # max terms per model (counts fixed terms and interactions)
MAX_MAIN <- NA   # max main effects per model, interactions not counted; NA = off.
                 # Use with INTERACTIONS, e.g. MAX_MAIN = 3 and M_MAX = 7 for a
                 # full 3-way. Much slower (~2 min per dredge with ~22
                 # predictors), so raise N_CORES or lower N_PERM.
RANK <- "AICc"   # "AICc", "AIC" or "BIC"
DELTA_TOP <- 2   # "top set" = models within this many units of the best

## ============================================================================
## Responses
## ============================================================================
CH4_TRANSFORM <- "log_shift" # "log_shift" = log(CH4 + c); "asinh" = asinh(CH4 / s)
SHIFT_ADD <- 0.02            # c = |min(CH4)| + SHIFT_ADD
ASINH_SCALE <- 0.02          # s

## ============================================================================
## Checks against selection on noise
## ============================================================================
N_PERM <- 100       # permutations of the response (0 = skip)
CV_SCHEME <- "loo"  # "loo" (leave one site out), "spatial" (leave out a group
                    # of sites within CV_BLOCK_KM of each other), "ecoregion"
                    # (leave out one ecoregion), or "none"
CV_BLOCK_KM <- 25   # spatial group size for CV_SCHEME = "spatial"
CV_PREDICT <- "best" # "best" = top model of each fold; "average" = model
                     # average of that fold's top set (delta < DELTA_TOP)

N_CORES <- min(8, parallel::detectCores()) # parallel workers for perm and CV; 1 = serial
SEED <- 1

## ============================================================================
## Candidate formulas (Section 6): hand-picked models, checked one by one
## ============================================================================
## Named list of formulas. Response: CH4_resp (CH4 under CH4_TRANSFORM) or
## CO2. Predictors: any short name loaded in Section 1, not just the
## screened pool; all are standardized. list() skips Section 6.
CANDIDATES <- list(
  `CH4 3-way` = CH4_resp ~ DMV_sd * WETprob_mean * era5_tmean_14d
)
## A candidate found by screening looks better than it is. The permutation
## test in Section 6.3 shuffles the response and repeats a screen like yours:
## the best full-interaction model (a * b * ...) of any CAND_SEARCH_K
## predictors from CAND_SEARCH_POOL. Match these to how you actually screened.
CAND_SEARCH_K <- 3          # predictors per screened model; 0 = skip the test
CAND_SEARCH_POOL <- "pool"  # "pool" = screened pool (Section 2); "all" = all
CAND_N_PERM <- 200
```

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(MuMIn)
library(parallel)

options(na.action = "na.fail") # dredge requires this

RASTER_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_RasterPredictors.csv")
CLIMATE_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv")
SITES_GPKG <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Sites_EcoEPA_6347.gpkg")

RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG") # reproducible random streams across parallel workers
set.seed(SEED)

INTERACTIONS <- INTERACTIONS[nzchar(INTERACTIONS)] # tolerate e.g. character(3)

stopifnot(
  CAND_SEARCH_POOL %in% c("pool", "all"),
  CH4_TRANSFORM %in% c("log_shift", "asinh"),
  CV_SCHEME %in% c("loo", "spatial", "ecoregion", "none"),
  CV_PREDICT %in% c("best", "average"),
  RANK %in% c("AICc", "AIC", "BIC")
)

## --- Plot styling (same palette as the other GHG notebooks) -----------------
WT_COLS <- c(EM = "#2a78d6", FO = "#eb6834", SS = "#1baf7a")
WT_SHAPES <- c(EM = 16, FO = 17, SS = 15)
RESP_COLS <- c(CH4 = "#2a78d6", CO2 = "#eb6834")
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          legend.position = "top")
)
```

## 1. Data

```{r load}
short_clim <- function(x) {
  x |> sub("total_precipitation_sum", "ppt", x = _) |>
    sub("temperature_2m", "tmean", x = _)
}

raster_cols <- c(outer(RASTER_BANDS, RASTER_STATS, \(b, s) sprintf("%s_%s_%dm", b, s, WINDOW)))
raster_short <- sub(sprintf("_%dm$", WINDOW), "", raster_cols)
clim_short <- short_clim(CLIMATE_VARS)

flux_site <- st_read(SITES_GPKG, quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(CH4 = mean(CH4_avg), CO2 = mean(CO2_avg), .groups = "drop")

clim_site <- read.csv(CLIMATE_CSV) |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(CLIMATE_VARS), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  rename_with(short_clim, -Site_ID)

dat <- read.csv(RASTER_CSV, colClasses = c(huc12 = "character")) |>
  select(Site_ID, Ecoregion, Wetland_Type, x, y, all_of(raster_cols)) |>
  rename_with(\(v) sub(sprintf("_%dm$", WINDOW), "", v)) |>
  left_join(flux_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  left_join(clim_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  mutate(Ecoregion = factor(Ecoregion),
         Wetland_Type = factor(Wetland_Type, levels = names(WT_COLS)))

stopifnot(nrow(dat) == 48, !anyNA(dat))

## Response transforms
ch4_shift <- abs(min(dat$CH4)) + SHIFT_ADD
dat$CH4_resp <- switch(CH4_TRANSFORM,
  log_shift = log(dat$CH4 + ch4_shift),
  asinh = asinh(dat$CH4 / ASINH_SCALE)
)
RESPONSES <- c(CH4 = "CH4_resp", CO2 = "CO2")
RESP_LABELS <- c(CH4 = sprintf("CH4 (%s)", sub("_", " ", CH4_TRANSFORM)), CO2 = "CO2")

all_preds <- setdiff(c(raster_short, clim_short), EXCLUDE)
stopifnot(all(c(PROTECT, FIXED) %in% all_preds))
```

## 2. Candidate pool

### 2.1 VIF screen

Predictors are standardized (mean 0, SD 1), so coefficients are per 1 SD.
Standardizing doesn't change any model's fit or predictions. It also doesn't
leak information between CV folds, because a linear model's predictions don't
change under a linear rescaling of its predictors.

```{r vif}
int_mains <- unique(unlist(strsplit(INTERACTIONS, ":", fixed = TRUE)))
stopifnot(all(int_mains %in% all_preds))
protected <- unique(c(PROTECT, FIXED, int_mains))

vif_of <- function(X) {
  v <- tryCatch(diag(solve(cor(X))), error = function(e) rep(Inf, ncol(X)))
  setNames(v, colnames(X))
}

## Drop exact linear combinations, then the highest-VIF unprotected predictor
## until every VIF is below `thresh`
vif_stepdown <- function(X, thresh, protected) {
  log <- tibble(step = integer(), dropped = character(), vif = numeric())
  q <- qr(scale(X), tol = 1e-7)
  if (q$rank < ncol(X)) {
    aliased <- setdiff(colnames(X)[q$pivot[-seq_len(q$rank)]], protected)
    log <- add_row(log, step = seq_along(aliased), dropped = aliased, vif = Inf)
    X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), aliased), drop = FALSE]
  }
  repeat {
    v <- vif_of(X)
    cand <- v[setdiff(names(v), protected)]
    if (!is.finite(thresh) || length(cand) == 0 || max(v) < thresh || ncol(X) <= 2) break
    worst <- names(which.max(cand))
    log <- add_row(log, step = nrow(log) + 1L, dropped = worst, vif = max(cand))
    X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), worst), drop = FALSE]
  }
  list(dropped = log, vif = v)
}

vs <- vif_stepdown(as.matrix(dat[all_preds]), VIF_MAX, protected)
POOL <- names(vs$vif)

## Standardized copies of the pool, overwriting the raw columns in `mdat`
mdat <- dat |> mutate(across(all_of(POOL), \(v) as.numeric(scale(v))))

if (nrow(vs$dropped)) {
  kable(vs$dropped, digits = 2, caption = sprintf("Dropped by the VIF screen (VIF_MAX = %s)", VIF_MAX))
}
tibble(predictor = POOL, VIF = vs$vif, protected = POOL %in% protected) |>
  arrange(desc(VIF)) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = sprintf("Candidate pool: %d predictors", length(POOL)))
```

### 2.2 Correlated pairs kept apart

```{r cor-pairs}
rho <- cor(mdat[POOL], method = "spearman")
idx <- which(abs(rho) >= COR_MAX & upper.tri(rho), arr.ind = TRUE)
cor_pairs <- tibble(a = rownames(rho)[idx[, 1]], b = colnames(rho)[idx[, 2]],
                    rho = rho[idx]) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(rho)))

## dredge subset matrix: FALSE = these two terms may not share a model.
## MuMIn reads only the lower triangle.
subset_mat <- abs(rho) < COR_MAX
subset_mat[!lower.tri(subset_mat)] <- NA

if (nrow(cor_pairs)) {
  kable(cor_pairs, digits = 2,
        caption = sprintf("Pairs with |ρ| ≥ %.2f: never in the same model", COR_MAX))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("No pairs with |rho| >= %.2f.\n", COR_MAX))
}
```

## 3. Dredge

```{r dredge-fns}
## Global model for one response
global_formula <- function(resp) {
  reformulate(c(POOL, INTERACTIONS), response = resp)
}

## Which term combinations dredge may fit. Without MAX_MAIN, a logical matrix
## keeps correlated pairs apart (fast). With MAX_MAIN, one expression does
## both: at most MAX_MAIN main effects, and no correlated pair.
dredge_subset <- if (!is.na(MAX_MAIN)) {
  mains <- setdiff(POOL, FIXED)
  str2lang(paste(c(
    sprintf("(%s) <= %d", paste0("`", mains, "`", collapse = " + "), MAX_MAIN),
    sprintf("!(`%s` & `%s`)", cor_pairs$a, cor_pairs$b)
  ), collapse = " & "))
} else if (nrow(cor_pairs)) {
  subset_mat
}

## Dredge one response on one data set. The formula and data are inlined
## into the lm() call, so dredge and get.models() can re-fit any sub-model
## from any environment (in a CV fold, in a forked worker, or later chunks).
run_dredge <- function(resp, d) {
  g <- eval(bquote(lm(.(global_formula(resp)), data = .(d))))
  ## bquote so the rank column is named after RANK ("AICc"), not "RANK"
  suppressMessages(eval(bquote(
    dredge(g, rank = .(RANK), m.lim = c(M_MIN, M_MAX),
           fixed = .(if (length(FIXED)) FIXED else NULL),
           subset = .(dredge_subset))
  )))
}

## Parallel map for the permutation tests and CV.
## * Forking (mclapply) is fastest, but some IDEs forbid it (Positron:
##   "Can't fork the R session"). CAN_FORK tests this once.
## * Otherwise a socket (PSOCK) cluster of fresh R sessions is used. Those
##   sessions start empty, so each call names the global objects FUN needs
##   in `export`; packages and options are set up when the cluster starts.
## * N_CORES = 1 runs serially.
CAN_FORK <- .Platform$OS.type == "unix" && tryCatch({
  mccollect(mcparallel(TRUE))
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) FALSE)

par_cl <- NULL # socket cluster, started on first use

## Globals used by run_dredge() and the helpers below
DREDGE_EXPORTS <- c("mdat", "run_dredge", "global_formula", "dredge_subset",
                    "POOL", "INTERACTIONS", "FIXED", "RANK", "M_MIN", "M_MAX",
                    "terms_in", "cand_terms", "null_gain")

par_map <- function(X, FUN, export = character()) {
  if (N_CORES <= 1) return(lapply(X, FUN))
  if (CAN_FORK) {
    out <- mclapply(X, FUN, mc.cores = N_CORES, mc.set.seed = TRUE)
    ## mclapply returns worker errors as "try-error" objects; stop on the first
    err <- keep(out, \(o) inherits(o, "try-error"))
    if (length(err)) stop("worker failed: ", err[[1]])
    return(out)
  }
  if (is.null(par_cl)) {
    par_cl <<- makeCluster(N_CORES)
    clusterEvalQ(par_cl, {
      suppressPackageStartupMessages({
        library(dplyr)
        library(purrr)
        library(MuMIn)
      })
      options(na.action = "na.fail")
    })
    clusterSetRNGStream(par_cl, SEED)
  }
  clusterExport(par_cl, export, envir = globalenv())
  parLapply(par_cl, X, FUN)
}

cat(if (N_CORES <= 1) "Serial" else if (CAN_FORK) "Forked" else "Socket-cluster",
    "parallel backend,", N_CORES, "cores\n")

## Terms that dredge can switch on and off (the fixed ones are always in)
## Labels are taken from the fitted global model, because R may reorder an
## interaction's variables ("a:b" can become "b:a").
cand_terms <- setdiff(attr(terms(global_formula("CO2")), "term.labels"), FIXED)

## Terms in each row of a model.selection table
terms_in <- function(dd) {
  cols <- intersect(cand_terms, names(dd))
  apply(!is.na(as.data.frame(dd)[cols]), 1, \(r) cols[r], simplify = FALSE)
}

## Rank-criterion gain of the best model over the null (fixed terms only)
null_gain <- function(dd) {
  k <- lengths(terms_in(dd))
  if (!any(k == 0)) return(NA_real_)
  dd$delta[k == 0][1]
}

## "a + b", with fixed terms first in brackets: "[fixed] + a + b"
model_label <- function(tt) {
  fx <- if (length(FIXED)) sprintf("[%s]", paste(FIXED, collapse = " + ")) else character()
  map_chr(tt, \(t) {
    parts <- c(fx, t)
    if (length(parts)) paste(parts, collapse = " + ") else "(null)"
  })
}
```

```{r dredge-run}
dd_list <- map(RESPONSES, \(r) run_dredge(r, mdat))

tibble(response = RESP_LABELS[names(dd_list)],
       models_fitted = map_int(dd_list, nrow),
       top_set = map_int(dd_list, \(dd) sum(dd$delta < DELTA_TOP)),
       best_model = map_chr(dd_list, \(dd) model_label(terms_in(dd)[1])),
       best_weight = map_dbl(dd_list, \(dd) dd$weight[1]),
       null_rank = map_int(dd_list, \(dd) which(lengths(terms_in(dd)) == 0)[1]),
       null_delta = map_dbl(dd_list, null_gain)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Dredge summary (%s, at most %d terms)", RANK, M_MAX))
```

### 3.1 Top model sets

Models within `r DELTA_TOP` `r RANK` units of the best. A long top set with
no clear winner means the data don't separate the candidate predictors.

```{r top-sets, results = "asis"}
for (nm in names(dd_list)) {
  dd <- dd_list[[nm]]
  top <- dd[dd$delta < DELTA_TOP, ]
  tibble(model = model_label(terms_in(top)), df = top$df,
         R2 = map_dbl(get.models(top, subset = TRUE), \(m) summary(m)$r.squared),
         !!RANK := top[[RANK]], delta = top$delta, weight = top$weight) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: top set (delta < %g)", RESP_LABELS[nm], DELTA_TOP)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### 3.2 Predictor importance (summed weights)

Each predictor's summed Akaike weight over **all** models that contain it.
Because the pool, the correlated-pair rule and `M_MAX` restrict which models
exist, these sums are relative to that model set, not absolute
probabilities. As a reference, the dashed line shows a predictor's expected
sum if every model had equal weight. It is drawn for each response, as the
model set can differ with `FIXED`.

```{r importance, fig.height=6}
imp <- imap_dfr(dd_list, function(dd, nm) {
  tt <- terms_in(dd)
  tibble(response = nm, term = cand_terms,
         sw = map_dbl(cand_terms, \(t) sum(dd$weight[map_lgl(tt, \(x) t %in% x)])),
         equal_w = map_dbl(cand_terms, \(t) mean(map_lgl(tt, \(x) t %in% x))))
})

imp_order <- imp |> group_by(term) |> summarise(m = max(sw)) |> arrange(m) |> pull(term)

ggplot(imp, aes(sw, factor(term, levels = imp_order))) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = response), width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(x = equal_w), shape = 124, size = 4, color = "#3a3936") +
  facet_wrap(~response, labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = RESP_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(title = "Summed model weight per predictor",
       subtitle = "Tick = expected sum if all models were equally supported",
       x = "Summed weight", y = NULL)
```

### 3.3 Coefficients: top model and model average

The model average is taken over the top set and uses the *full* average:
terms absent from a model count as 0, which shrinks weakly supported terms
toward 0. Intervals are shown for reference only. They do not account for
the selection step, so they are too narrow.

```{r coefs, fig.height=6}
coef_df <- imap_dfr(dd_list, function(dd, nm) {
  best <- get.models(dd, 1)[[1]]
  ci <- confint(best)
  out <- tibble(response = nm, model = "top model", term = names(coef(best)),
                estimate = unname(coef(best)), lo = ci[, 1], hi = ci[, 2])
  if (sum(dd$delta < DELTA_TOP) > 1) {
    av <- model.avg(dd, subset = delta < DELTA_TOP)
    cf <- coef(av, full = TRUE)
    ci <- confint(av, full = TRUE)
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(response = nm, model = "top-set average", term = names(cf),
                                 estimate = unname(cf), lo = ci[names(cf), 1], hi = ci[names(cf), 2]))
  }
  out
}) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")

ggplot(coef_df, aes(estimate, term, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free_x", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`top model` = "#2a78d6", `top-set average` = "#898781")) +
  labs(title = "Coefficients per 1 SD of each predictor",
       subtitle = "95% intervals, not adjusted for model selection",
       x = "Estimate", y = NULL, color = NULL)
```

### 3.4 Top-model diagnostics

```{r diag, fig.height=6}
diag_d <- imap_dfr(dd_list, function(dd, nm) {
  m <- get.models(dd, 1)[[1]]
  tibble(response = nm, fitted = fitted(m), resid = residuals(m),
         Wetland_Type = mdat$Wetland_Type)
})

rf <- ggplot(diag_d, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
  labs(title = "Top model: residuals vs fitted", x = "Fitted", y = "Residual",
       color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")

qq <- ggplot(diag_d, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  stat_qq(size = 1.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  labs(title = "Residual normal Q-Q", x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")

rf / qq
```

## 4. Is the selected model better than chance?

### 4.1 Permutation test

Shuffling the response breaks any link to the predictors but keeps its
distribution and the predictors' correlations. Dredge is then re-run with the
same settings. The statistic is the null model's delta: how many `r RANK`
units the best model beats the null by. The p-value is the share of shuffles
whose best model beats the null by at least as much as the real data's.

```{r perm}
perm_res <- if (N_PERM > 0) {
  imap(RESPONSES, function(r, nm) {
    obs <- null_gain(dd_list[[nm]])
    perm <- unlist(par_map(seq_len(N_PERM), function(i) {
      d <- mdat
      d[[r]] <- sample(d[[r]])
      null_gain(run_dredge(r, d))
    }, export = DREDGE_EXPORTS))
    list(obs = obs, perm = perm, p = (sum(perm >= obs) + 1) / (N_PERM + 1))
  })
}
```

```{r perm-plot, fig.height=4}
if (N_PERM > 0) {
  perm_long <- imap_dfr(perm_res, \(p, nm) tibble(response = nm, gain = p$perm))
  perm_obs <- imap_dfr(perm_res, \(p, nm) tibble(
    response = nm, gain = p$obs,
    lab = sprintf("observed = %.1f\np = %.3f", p$obs, p$p)))

  print(
    ggplot(perm_long, aes(gain)) +
      geom_histogram(aes(fill = response), bins = 25, color = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_vline(data = perm_obs, aes(xintercept = gain), color = "#3a3936", linewidth = 0.8) +
      geom_text(data = perm_obs, aes(x = gain, y = Inf, label = lab),
                hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.3, size = 3.3, color = "#3a3936") +
      facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = RESP_COLS) +
      labs(title = sprintf("Best-model gain over the null: real data vs %d shuffles", N_PERM),
           x = sprintf("Null model delta %s", RANK), y = "Shuffles")
  )
}
```

### 4.2 Nested cross-validation

In each fold, everything in Section 3 is re-run on the training sites only.
The model it selects then predicts the held-out sites. The baseline
prediction is the training-fold mean. **Predictive R² ≤ 0 means the selected
models predict new sites no better than that mean.** For CH4 the errors are on
the transformed scale.

Folds: `r CV_SCHEME`. With `"spatial"`, sites are grouped by complete-linkage
clustering so that every pair in a group is within `r CV_BLOCK_KM` km. That
keeps nearby, similar sites out of the training data for each other.

```{r cv-folds}
cv_folds <- switch(CV_SCHEME,
  loo = seq_len(nrow(mdat)),
  spatial = cutree(hclust(dist(mdat[c("x", "y")]) / 1000, method = "complete"), h = CV_BLOCK_KM),
  ecoregion = as.integer(mdat$Ecoregion),
  none = NULL
)
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  cat(sprintf("%d folds; held-out sites per fold: min %d, median %g, max %d\n",
              n_distinct(cv_folds), min(table(cv_folds)), median(table(cv_folds)),
              max(table(cv_folds))))
}
```

```{r cv}
predict_fold <- function(dd, newdata) {
  if (CV_PREDICT == "average" && sum(dd$delta < DELTA_TOP) > 1) {
    predict(model.avg(get.models(dd, subset = delta < DELTA_TOP)), newdata = newdata, full = TRUE)
  } else {
    predict(get.models(dd, 1)[[1]], newdata = newdata)
  }
}

cv_res <- if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  imap(RESPONSES, function(r, nm) {
    folds <- par_map(sort(unique(cv_folds)), function(k) {
      test <- cv_folds == k
      dd <- run_dredge(r, mdat[!test, ])
      list(pred = tibble(row = which(test), pred = unname(predict_fold(dd, mdat[test, ])),
                         base = mean(mdat[[r]][!test])),
           terms = terms_in(dd)[[1]])
    }, export = c(DREDGE_EXPORTS, "cv_folds", "predict_fold", "CV_PREDICT", "DELTA_TOP"))
    pred <- map_dfr(folds, "pred") |>
      arrange(row) |>
      mutate(obs = mdat[[r]][row], Wetland_Type = mdat$Wetland_Type[row])
    list(pred = pred, terms = map(folds, "terms"))
  })
}
```

```{r cv-table}
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  imap_dfr(cv_res, \(cv, nm) with(cv$pred, tibble(
    response = RESP_LABELS[nm],
    RMSE_selected = sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2)),
    RMSE_mean = sqrt(mean((obs - base)^2)),
    predictive_R2 = 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - base)^2),
    in_sample_R2 = summary(get.models(dd_list[[nm]], 1)[[1]])$r.squared
  ))) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Nested CV (%s folds, %s prediction)", CV_SCHEME, CV_PREDICT))
}
```

```{r cv-plot, fig.height=4.5}
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  cvp <- imap_dfr(cv_res, \(cv, nm) mutate(cv$pred, response = nm))
  ggplot(cvp, aes(obs, pred)) +
    geom_abline(color = "#c3c2b7") +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = mean(obs)), color = "#c3c2b7", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
    labs(title = "Held-out predictions from the nested CV",
         subtitle = "Solid = 1:1; dashed = mean of observed",
         x = "Observed", y = "Predicted (held out)",
         color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
}
```

### 4.3 Selection stability across folds

How often each predictor is in the best model of a CV fold. A real effect is
picked in most folds. A predictor picked in only a few folds was chosen
because of particular sites.

```{r stability, fig.height=5}
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  stab <- imap_dfr(cv_res, function(cv, nm) {
    tibble(response = nm, term = cand_terms,
           freq = map_dbl(cand_terms, \(t) mean(map_lgl(cv$terms, \(x) t %in% x))))
  }) |>
    group_by(term) |> filter(max(freq) > 0) |> ungroup()

  stab_order <- stab |> group_by(term) |> summarise(m = max(freq)) |> arrange(m) |> pull(term)

  print(
    ggplot(stab, aes(freq, factor(term, levels = stab_order))) +
      geom_col(aes(fill = response), width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
      facet_wrap(~response, labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = RESP_COLS) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
      labs(title = "Share of CV folds whose best model includes each predictor",
           subtitle = "Predictors never selected are omitted", x = NULL, y = NULL)
  )

  imap_dfr(cv_res, \(cv, nm) tibble(response = RESP_LABELS[nm], model = model_label(cv$terms))) |>
    count(response, model, sort = TRUE) |>
    group_by(response) |> slice_head(n = 5) |> ungroup() |>
    kable(caption = "Most common best models across CV folds (top 5 per response)")
}
```

## 5. Summary

```{r summary}
tibble(
  response = RESP_LABELS[names(dd_list)],
  best_model = map_chr(dd_list, \(dd) model_label(terms_in(dd)[1])),
  in_sample_R2 = map_dbl(dd_list, \(dd) summary(get.models(dd, 1)[[1]])$r.squared),
  gain_over_null = map_dbl(dd_list, null_gain),
  perm_p = if (N_PERM > 0) map_dbl(perm_res, "p") else NA_real_,
  cv_R2 = if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
    map_dbl(cv_res, \(cv) with(cv$pred, 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - base)^2)))
  } else NA_real_
) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Does the dredge selection hold up?")

cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "Settings: window %d m; pool %d predictors (VIF < %s, |rho| < %s apart); ",
  "%s; %d-%d terms (max %s main effects); %d interactions; %d fixed; ",
  "%d permutations; CV %s (%s)\n"),
  WINDOW, length(POOL), VIF_MAX, COR_MAX, RANK, M_MIN, M_MAX,
  if (is.na(MAX_MAIN)) "-" else MAX_MAIN, length(INTERACTIONS),
  length(FIXED), N_PERM, CV_SCHEME, CV_PREDICT))
```

A selection worth carrying forward needs a small permutation p **and** a
positive cross-validated R². For CO2 or CH4, take a selected predictor to
`GHG_Model_SiteMeans.qmd` only if it is also selected in most CV folds
(Section 4.3).

## 6. Candidate formulas

Hand-picked models from `CANDIDATES`, for example ones found by preliminary
screening. Each is checked as a fixed formula:

* **6.1 Comparison:** fit and cross-validation against the null model, the
  same predictors without interactions, and dredge's best model.
* **6.2 Terms:** F-tests of the highest-order terms, and coefficients.
* **6.3 Search-adjusted test:** how often a screen like yours finds an R² this
  high when the response is shuffled.
* **6.4 Influence:** sites with high leverage, and whether the top-order terms
  survive dropping any one site.
* **6.5 Interaction plots:** fitted surfaces, with the sites behind them.

The in-sample numbers in 6.1 and 6.2 (R², AICc, F-test p) assume the formula
was chosen before seeing the data. For a screened candidate they are too
optimistic. The cross-validation in 6.1 is optimistic too, because the
formula was picked using all sites; only the screen in 6.3 is repeated on
the shuffled data. Section 6.3 is the honest test.

```{r cand-setup, eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0}
## Every predictor standardized (not only the pool), for any candidate
cdat <- dat |> mutate(across(all_of(all_preds), \(v) as.numeric(scale(v))))

cand_resp <- function(f) all.vars(f[[2]])
cand_vars <- function(f) all.vars(f[[3]])
resp_name <- function(f) names(RESPONSES)[RESPONSES == cand_resp(f)]

walk(CANDIDATES, function(f) {
  stopifnot(cand_resp(f) %in% RESPONSES)
  bad <- setdiff(cand_vars(f), names(cdat))
  if (length(bad)) stop("unknown predictor(s): ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
})

## Highest-order terms of a model (e.g. the 3-way term of a * b * c)
top_terms <- function(m) {
  tt <- terms(m)
  attr(tt, "term.labels")[attr(tt, "order") == max(attr(tt, "order"))]
}

## Fixed-formula CV: refit in each fold, predict held-out sites
cand_folds <- list(
  loo = seq_len(nrow(cdat)),
  spatial = cutree(hclust(dist(cdat[c("x", "y")]) / 1000, method = "complete"), h = CV_BLOCK_KM),
  ecoregion = as.integer(cdat$Ecoregion)
)
cv_fixed <- function(f, folds) {
  y <- cdat[[cand_resp(f)]]
  pred <- base <- numeric(length(y))
  for (k in unique(folds)) {
    test <- folds == k
    pred[test] <- predict(lm(f, data = cdat[!test, ]), newdata = cdat[test, ])
    base[test] <- mean(y[!test])
  }
  1 - sum((y - pred)^2) / sum((y - base)^2)
}

cand_fits <- map(CANDIDATES, \(f) lm(f, data = cdat))
```

### 6.1 Comparison with simpler models

`k` is the number of coefficients. Cross-validated R² ≤ 0 means no better
than predicting the training-fold mean. `spatial` holds out groups of sites
within `r CV_BLOCK_KM` km; `ecoregion` holds out one ecoregion at a time.

```{r cand-compare, results = "asis", eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0}
iwalk(CANDIDATES, function(f, nm) {
  r <- cand_resp(f)
  comp <- list(
    `null` = reformulate("1", response = r),
    `main effects only` = reformulate(cand_vars(f), response = r),
    `dredge best` = formula(get.models(dd_list[[resp_name(f)]], 1)[[1]]),
    candidate = f
  )
  comp <- comp[!duplicated(map_chr(comp, \(x) paste(deparse(x), collapse = "")))]
  imap_dfr(comp, function(fc, lab) {
    m <- lm(fc, data = cdat)
    tibble(model = lab, formula = paste(deparse(fc[[3]], width.cutoff = 500), collapse = ""),
           k = length(coef(m)), sites_per_coef = nrow(cdat) / k,
           R2 = summary(m)$r.squared, adj_R2 = summary(m)$adj.r.squared, AICc = AICc(m),
           cv_loo = cv_fixed(fc, cand_folds$loo),
           cv_spatial = cv_fixed(fc, cand_folds$spatial),
           cv_ecoregion = cv_fixed(fc, cand_folds$ecoregion))
  }) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s (%s): comparison", nm, RESP_LABELS[resp_name(f)])) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
})
```

### 6.2 Terms

`drop1` F-tests remove each highest-order term in turn. Lower-order terms are
only tested once nothing above them depends on them, so these respect
marginality.

```{r cand-terms, results = "asis", eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0}
iwalk(cand_fits, function(m, nm) {
  d1 <- drop1(m, test = "F")
  tibble(term = rownames(d1)[-1], df = d1$Df[-1], F = d1$`F value`[-1], p = d1$`Pr(>F)`[-1]) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: F-tests of the highest-order terms", nm)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
  cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  tibble(term = rownames(cf), estimate = cf[, 1], SE = cf[, 2], t = cf[, 3], p = cf[, 4]) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: coefficients (per 1 SD)", nm)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
})
```

### 6.3 Search-adjusted permutation test

The screen: fit `a * b * ...` (all interactions) for every set of
`r CAND_SEARCH_K` predictors from the `r CAND_SEARCH_POOL` set, and keep the
highest R². On the real data that best R² is at least the candidate's (if the
candidate is one of the screened models). On shuffled data it shows how high
the best R² gets by chance. **p = share of shuffles whose best screened R²
reaches the candidate's R².** If you screened differently (other predictors,
other model forms, or other responses too), set `CAND_SEARCH_K` and
`CAND_SEARCH_POOL` to match. If you can't match it, treat p as a lower bound.

```{r cand-perm, eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0 && CAND_SEARCH_K > 0}
search_vars <- if (CAND_SEARCH_POOL == "all") all_preds else POOL
search_sets <- combn(search_vars, CAND_SEARCH_K, simplify = FALSE)

## QR of each screened design matrix, computed once; for any response vector
## the residuals are then one qr.resid() call per model
search_qr <- map(search_sets, \(v) qr(model.matrix(
  reformulate(paste(sprintf("`%s`", v), collapse = " * ")), cdat)))

search_r2 <- function(y) {
  tss <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  map_dbl(search_qr, \(q) 1 - sum(qr.resid(q, y)^2) / tss)
}

## One permutation distribution per response used by a candidate
cand_perm <- map(set_names(unique(map_chr(CANDIDATES, cand_resp))), function(r) {
  y <- cdat[[r]]
  list(obs = search_r2(y),
       perm = unlist(par_map(seq_len(CAND_N_PERM), \(i) max(search_r2(sample(y))),
                             export = c("search_r2", "search_qr"))))
})

imap_dfr(cand_fits, function(m, nm) {
  cp <- cand_perm[[cand_resp(formula(m))]]
  r2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  tibble(candidate = nm, models_screened = length(search_qr), candidate_R2 = r2,
         rank_on_real_data = sum(cp$obs > r2 + 1e-12) + 1,
         best_screened_R2 = max(cp$obs),
         shuffled_best_median = median(cp$perm),
         shuffled_best_95 = quantile(cp$perm, 0.95),
         p = (sum(cp$perm >= r2) + 1) / (CAND_N_PERM + 1))
}) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf(
    "Best of %d screened %d-predictor interaction models: real vs %d shuffles",
    length(search_qr), CAND_SEARCH_K, CAND_N_PERM))
```

```{r cand-perm-plot, fig.height=3.5, eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0 && CAND_SEARCH_K > 0}
cand_r2 <- imap_dfr(cand_fits, \(m, nm) tibble(
  candidate = nm, response = cand_resp(formula(m)), R2 = summary(m)$r.squared))

imap_dfr(cand_perm, \(cp, r) tibble(response = r, best_R2 = cp$perm)) |>
  inner_join(cand_r2, by = "response", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  ggplot(aes(best_R2)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#898781", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = R2), color = "#2a78d6", linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~candidate, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Best screened R² on shuffled responses",
       subtitle = "Blue line = the candidate's R² on the real data",
       x = "Best R² among screened models", y = "Shuffles")
```

### 6.4 Influence

Leverage above 2k/n is flagged as high. A site with leverage near 1 has the
fitted surface pass almost through it. The drop-one refits show whether the
highest-order terms depend on single sites.

```{r cand-influence, results = "asis", eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0}
cand_drop1 <- imap(cand_fits, function(m, nm) {
  f <- formula(m)
  k <- length(coef(m))
  infl <- tibble(Site_ID = dat$Site_ID, Wetland_Type = dat$Wetland_Type,
                 leverage = hatvalues(m), cooks_D = cooks.distance(m)) |>
    bind_cols(dat[cand_vars(f)])
  infl |>
    arrange(desc(cooks_D)) |>
    slice_head(n = 5) |>
    mutate(high_leverage = leverage > 2 * k / nrow(dat)) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf(
      "%s: five most influential sites (Cook's D; raw predictor values; 2k/n = %.2f)",
      nm, 2 * k / nrow(dat))) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")

  tops <- top_terms(m)
  drops <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(cdat)), function(i) {
    cf <- summary(lm(f, data = cdat[-i, ]))$coefficients
    tibble(dropped = dat$Site_ID[i], term = tops,
           estimate = cf[tops, 1], p = cf[tops, 4])
  })
  drops |>
    group_by(term) |>
    summarise(p_all_sites = summary(m)$coefficients[term[1], 4],
              p_median = median(p), p_max = max(p),
              share_p_below_0.05 = mean(p < 0.05),
              sign_flips = sum(sign(estimate) != sign(coef(m)[term[1]])),
              worst_drop = dropped[which.max(p)], .groups = "drop") |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: highest-order terms when each site is dropped in turn", nm)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
  mutate(drops, candidate = nm)
})
```

```{r cand-drop1-plot, fig.height=4, eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0}
bind_rows(cand_drop1) |>
  ggplot(aes(p, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, color = "#e34948", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.15, width = 0, size = 1.6, alpha = 0.7, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~candidate, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Highest-order term p-values with each site dropped in turn",
       subtitle = "One point per dropped site; dashed line = 0.05",
       x = "p (log scale)", y = NULL)
```

### 6.5 Interaction plots

For candidates with interactions among 2 or 3 predictors. Predictions vary
the first predictor along the x axis and hold the second (colours) and third
(panels) at their 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles. Points are the sites in
each panel's third of the third predictor. Lines span regions with few or no
sites, so the right-hand plot shows where the data are. Predictions are on
the model scale (transformed CH4).

```{r cand-int-plots, fig.height=5.5, eval = length(CANDIDATES) > 0}
pct_lab <- c("10th", "50th", "90th")

iwalk(cand_fits, function(m, nm) {
  f <- formula(m)
  v <- cand_vars(f)
  if (max(attr(terms(m), "order")) < 2 || !length(v) %in% 2:3) return(invisible())
  r <- cand_resp(f)
  if (length(v) == 2) v[3] <- NA
  to_raw <- \(z, var) z * sd(dat[[var]]) + mean(dat[[var]])

  q2 <- quantile(cdat[[v[2]]], c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
  q3 <- if (is.na(v[3])) 0 else quantile(cdat[[v[3]]], c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
  grid <- expand_grid(x = seq(min(cdat[[v[1]]]), max(cdat[[v[1]]]), length.out = 60),
                      i2 = 1:3, i3 = seq_along(q3)) |>
    mutate(!!v[1] := x, !!v[2] := q2[i2])
  if (!is.na(v[3])) grid[[v[3]]] <- q3[grid$i3]
  pr <- predict(m, newdata = grid, interval = "confidence")
  grid <- grid |>
    mutate(fit = pr[, "fit"], lo = pr[, "lwr"], hi = pr[, "upr"],
           x_raw = to_raw(x, v[1]),
           col = factor(sprintf("%s %s (%.2f)", v[2], pct_lab[i2], to_raw(q2[i2], v[2])),
                        levels = unique(sprintf("%s %s (%.2f)", v[2], pct_lab, to_raw(q2, v[2])))))

  pts <- tibble(x_raw = dat[[v[1]]], y = cdat[[r]], v2 = dat[[v[2]]])
  if (!is.na(v[3])) {
    lab3 <- sprintf("%s %s (%.2f)", v[3], pct_lab, to_raw(q3, v[3]))
    grid$panel <- factor(lab3[grid$i3], levels = lab3)
    pts$panel <- factor(lab3[as.integer(cut(rank(cdat[[v[3]]], ties.method = "first"), 3))],
                        levels = lab3)
  }

  p_fit <- ggplot(grid, aes(x_raw, fit)) +
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(x_raw, y), color = "#c3c2b7", size = 1.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = col), alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_line(aes(color = col), linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#898781", "#eb6834")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#898781", "#eb6834")) +
    labs(title = sprintf("%s: fitted surface", nm), x = v[1], y = r, color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
  if (!is.na(v[3])) p_fit <- p_fit + facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1)

  p_dat <- ggplot(pts, aes(x_raw, v2)) +
    labs(title = "Where the sites are", x = v[1], y = v[2]) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  p_dat <- if (is.na(v[3])) {
    p_dat + geom_point(size = 2, color = "#2a78d6")
  } else {
    pts$v3 <- dat[[v[3]]]
    p_dat %+% pts + geom_point(aes(color = v3), size = 2) +
      scale_color_gradient(low = "#c3c2b7", high = "#2a78d6", name = v[3])
  }

  print(p_fit + p_dat + plot_layout(widths = c(3, 1)))
})
```
